subject.title: [Feature]: Add before_persistence_write hook for durable state changes

question: Should OpenClaw add a dedicated before_persistence_write Plugin SDK hook for durable writes, or represent durable-write policy through enriched existing hooks and provenance surfaces instead?
rationale: This choice defines a public plugin security boundary over persisted user and agent state, including what data plugins can see, whether plugins may block or mutate writes, and how hook failures affect durable state.

options.title: Design a dedicated durable-write hook
options.body: Add a narrow before_persistence_write contract with redacted targets, ordering, block or mutation rules, timeout/failure policy, docs, and representative writer coverage.

options.title: Fold durable context into existing hooks
options.body: Extend before_tool_call and provenance/read-time APIs instead of adding a new hook family, reducing hook count but requiring broader taxonomy work first.

options.title: Defer to provenance design
options.body: Keep this issue open as a dependency of the broader persistent-state provenance work until maintainers settle the end-to-end trust model.

recommendation.title: Design a dedicated durable-write hook
recommendation.body: Add a narrow before_persistence_write contract with redacted targets, ordering, block or mutation rules, timeout/failure policy, docs, and representative writer coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc has the strongest current hook-contract history and owns the adjacent operator-policy security discussion referenced by this request.
